item.title: Top 2 Democrats on Intel say they're preparing for Trump to claim foreign meddling
item.description: The top Democrats on the House and Senate intelligence committees said they are working under the presumption that the president will seek to justify election interference by alleging fraud.
item.content:encoded:
The top Democrats on the House and Senate intelligence committees said they are working under the presumption that the president will seek to justify election interference by alleging fraud.

(Image credit: Anna Moneymaker)

item.title: How Trump's attacks on voting system integrity might affect upcoming elections
item.description: Election law expert Rick Hasen explains Trump's interference in the midterms, including threatening local officials with criminal prosecution unless they strike alleged noncitizens from voter rolls.
item.content:encoded: Election law expert Rick Hasen explains Trump's interference in the midterms, including threatening local officials with criminal prosecution unless they strike alleged noncitizens from voter rolls.
item.dc:creator: Dave Davies

item.title: Why local officials are feeling 'on edge' as election day approaches
item.description: Al Schmidt is the chief election official in the state of Pennsylvania. President Trump's insults put him in danger during the 2020 ballot count. Now Schmidt talks about preparing for the midterms.
item.content:encoded: Al Schmidt is the chief election official in the state of Pennsylvania. President Trump's insults put him in danger during the 2020 ballot count. Now Schmidt talks about preparing for the midterms.

item.title: Supreme Court upholds pause on Trump's anti-trans prison policy
item.description: The Supreme Court ruled Wednesday that the Trump administration has to continue providing gender-affirming care to inmates in federal prisons as litigation on efforts to change the policy continues.
item.content:encoded:
The Supreme Court ruled Wednesday that the Trump administration has to continue providing gender-affirming care to inmates in federal prisons as litigation on efforts to change the policy continues.

(Image credit: Saul Loeb/AFP via Getty Images)

item.title: Trump leans into unprecedented power ahead of midterm elections
item.description: Less than two weeks before the election, Trump continues to crash through barriers that he wouldn't dare cross in his first term.

item.title: DOJ's noncitizen voter list is unreliable, officials say. And, U.S. pollution rises
item.description: The Justice Department's "likely" noncitizen voter list in California is "unreliable," according to officials. And, the United Nations reports a major increase in U.S. climate pollution.

item.title: Why Republicans frustrated with Trump's policies continue to support the party
item.description: NPR's Steve Inskeep asks Bloomberg politics columnist Ron Brownstein what motivates Republicans angry with the Trump administration to continue voting for the Republican party.

item.title: Trump to campaign for Sen. Darline Graham despite disagreement on Russia sanctions
item.description: President Trump is expected to campaign with Sen. Darline Graham on Wednesday even as the two are not in agreement on how to best pressure Russia to end the war in Ukraine.

item.title: Some on DOJ's 20,000 'likely' noncitizen list in California appear to be U.S.-born
item.description: Election officials in Los Angeles County say their preliminary analysis of the federal government's list of 20,000 "likely" noncitizens registered to vote in California shows the list is "unreliable."

item.title: Beef producers could play a big role in this year's midterm elections
item.description: Trump's policies have complicated his support among beef producers, a key constituency in states where tight Senate races could sway control of the body.
